extracted.intended_audience: practicing patent attorneys, patent owners, and USPTO examiners involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, filing, and prosecuting patent owner responses, supplemental replies, amendments, drawings, inventorship corrections, and excess-claims fees in inter partes reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and cited 37 CFR rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time requests — factual showing of diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for extension must state (A) when the action was taken and (B) why, despite that action, additional time is needed; statement (A) must provide a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by all those responsible for preparing a response within the statutory time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution initially sets a time period of at least 30 days or one month (whichever is longer). First requests for extensions will be granted for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time (usually 1 month). Reasons are evaluated; favorable consideration where factual accounting of reasonable diligence is shown. Second or subsequent requests, or requests for more than one month, will be granted only in extraordinary situations. See MPEP § 2662.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions to submit affidavits after ACP may be questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for extension states more time is needed to submit an affidavit and is filed after an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP), granting the extension is without prejudice to the examiner questioning why the affidavit is now necessary and why it was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner's showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding the grant of an extension. The grant merely gives an extended opportunity to present the affidavit or take other action. Affidavits submitted after an ACP are treated like amendments submitted after an ACP and may be refused entry (see In re Affidavit Filed After Final Rejection).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.111 — form and content of reply to non-final Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Reply must be reduced to writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner's action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out the specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the claim language distinguishes over the references does not comply. See 37 CFR 1.111(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies — limits and entry conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply supplemental to a reply in compliance with § 1.111(b) will not be entered as a matter of right except where clearly limited to specific categories (cancellation of claims; adoption of examiner suggestions; placement in condition for allowance; reply to a requirement made after the first reply; correction of informalities; simplification of issues for appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within the period during which action by the Office is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c). See 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(i)-(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies must be bona fide attempts to advance prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant's or patent owner's reply must appear throughout to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application or the reexamination proceeding to final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies that merely assert patentability without substance are inadequate. The full response should meaningfully advance prosecution by addressing grounds of rejection and providing distinctions over references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must point out patentable novelty and avoidance of references
rubrics_metrics.description: When amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant or patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed to be present in the claims in view of the art and must show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to amendments in both applications and reexaminations (see MPEP § 2666.01; 37 CFR 1.111(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.945 — response timing and supplemental response cause showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner will be given at least thirty days to file a response to any Office action on the merits of an inter partes reexamination. Any supplemental response will be entered only with a showing of sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The showing must include: (1) explanation of how § 1.111(a)(2)(i) requirements are satisfied; (2) explanation of why the supplemental response was not presented with the original response; and (3) a compelling reason to enter the supplemental response. If no sufficient cause is shown, the supplemental response will not be entered and may be sealed from public view in the IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination responses follow application examination rules (substance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings are conducted in accordance with §§ 1.104 through 1.116; accordingly, 37 CFR 1.111 applies to the patent owner's response in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for reconsideration must be in writing and distinctly point out each supposed error; reasons must state how claims define over references and why any 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections are incorrect or inapplicable. Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132 may be used subject to limitations (see below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit limitations — 1.131 cannot 'swear back' when reference claims same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 may not be used to 'swear back' of a reference patent if the reference patent is claiming the same invention as the patent undergoing reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that situation consider affidavit under 37 CFR 1.130 (see MPEP § 718), or raising the issue via interference/reissue if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No filing third-party papers on behalf of third party
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of a third party; if a third party paper accompanies a patent owner response, the combined submission is improper and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not separate the submission; the third-party paper filed as part of the owner's response will not be considered. Return the improper response using form PTOL-2069 and give the patent owner time to refile the response without the third-party paper. See MPEP § 2666.50.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on third-party requester and requester comment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the patent owner response must be served on the third party requester in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248; the requester must file written comments within 30 days from the date of service to be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of service may make requester comments untimely; where record does not show service, see MPEP § 2666.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response period and extensions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner will normally be given a period of two months to respond to an Office action in reexamination; an extension of time can be obtained only in accordance with 37 CFR 1.956.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that 37 CFR 1.136 does not apply in reexamination proceedings. See MPEP § 2666.10 for consequences of failure to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental response entry consequences and filing strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental response is not entered, it and any comments may be returned or discarded; if scanned into IFW and cannot be physically returned, they will be marked 'closed' and 'non-public' and will not constitute part of the reexamination record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental response not approved for entry will not be entered when a response to a subsequent Office action is filed, even if a specific request for entry is made in that subsequent response. To have an unentered supplemental considered, include its contents in a proper response to a subsequent Office action. If the next Office action closes prosecution, entry is governed by 37 CFR 1.116 (see 1.951(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application data sheet (ADS) is improper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner cannot submit an application data sheet (ADS) in a reexamination proceeding since a reexamination proceeding is not an 'application' (see 37 CFR 1.76).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ADS is an improper paper in a reexamination proceeding and should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by patent owner must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and 1.943
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in inter partes reexamination are made by filing a paper in compliance with §§ 1.530(d)-(k) and 1.943 and pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(j) manner-of-amendment rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.12 may be used to advise patent owner of proper manner; use form paragraph 26.05.01 to notify of noncompliance and set shortened statutory period (one month/30 days) to correct informality, with consequences per 37 CFR 1.957(b) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making specification amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification other than claims must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings, except an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting the paragraph without presenting its text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The precise insertion point must be identified. This applies whether amendment is submitted on paper or compact disc (see §§ 1.96 and 1.825).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making claim amendments — full text and markings required
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim being proposed to be changed and of each new claim proposed to be added; changed claims should have a parenthetical 'amended', 'twice amended', etc.; proposed added or changed claims must include markings except cancellation may be by statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim changed or added must include markings per 37 CFR 1.530(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making drawing amendments — sketches and formal sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; upon approval, new sheets complying with § 1.84 must be filed. Amended figures identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', canceled figures bracketed and identified as 'Canceled.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketches should be in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red; examiner may have draftsperson review substitute sheets. Draftsperson 'stamp' is no longer required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markings for added and omitted matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Matter to be omitted must be enclosed in brackets; matter to be added must be underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These markings apply to all changes relative to the patent being reexamined made to the specification and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering — no renumbering; added claims follow highest number
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. Numbering of any claims added must follow the number of the highest-numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain sequence; do not reorder existing claim numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not introduce new matter or enlarge claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent (other than cancellation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended or new claims which broaden or enlarge scope should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a). The test for enlargement under 35 U.S.C. 314(a) is the same as under 35 U.S.C. 251 (see In re Freeman). If the patent expires during reexamination, amendments are improper and reexamination continues on unamended claims. See handling of new matter at MPEP § 2670 and enlargement discussion at § 2658.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of proposed amendments — certificate issuance required
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments will be treated as though entered for prosecution purposes if timely and compliant, but are not effective in the patent until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Office actions treat proposed amendments as entered, they are not incorporated into the patent until the certificate is issued under 35 U.S.C. 316 (or other applicable statute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction is effected the same as in ex parte reexamination; Director may include an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s) in the reexamination certificate on petition of all parties and satisfactory proof and fee satisfying § 1.324 and § 1.20(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition satisfying § 1.324 is filed but the proceeding concludes other than by reexamination certificate, a certificate of correction indicating the change will be issued upon request by the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees in reexamination (37 CFR 1.20(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess-claims fees apply in reexamination for each independent claim in excess of 3 and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent (fee levels for small entities and others specified), and for each claim in excess of 20 and in excess of the number of claims in the patent (fees specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees listed (examples): independent-excess fee $105 small entity / $210 other; total-excess fee $25 small entity / $50 other. Fees are due 'on filing or on presentation at any other time' of excess claims (i.e., during reexamination). If fees are not paid with presentation, they must be paid or the claims canceled prior to expiration of time set for reply in a fee-deficiency notice to avoid abandonment. See 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2) and 37 CFR 1.20(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of excess claims fees — calculation rules and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent-excess fee applies only if amendment increases independent claims above both three and the number in the patent; the total-excess fee applies only if amendment increases total claims above both twenty and the number in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided illustrate different cancel/add scenarios (e.g., patent with 6 independent / 30 total claims): (A) cancel 10 and add 10 (no excess fee if counts remain within limits); (B) cancel 10 (2 independent) and add 10 (3 independent) — fee for seventh independent claim due; (C) cancel 10 and add 11 — fee for thirty-first claim due; (D) cancel 10 and add 11 with 3 independents added — both independent and total excess fees due. Claims disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 or canceled via prior reexamination/reissue/certificate of correction are not considered in fee calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay excess claim fees consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with the request or later presentation, the fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment or cancellation is required to avoid abandonment of the proceeding or the amendment.
